title: Black Chalk HiDE Extra Brut 2021 Hampshire, England
summary: Website: https://blackchalkwine.co.uk/products/hide-2021 This is a new single-vineyard sparkling wine from Black Chalk. It’s a very chalky block with shallow soils
content:
Website: https://blackchalkwine.co.uk/products/hide-2021

This is a new single-vineyard sparkling wine from Black Chalk. It’s a very chalky block with shallow soils and 50% stones in the soil, and it’s a blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir with just a trickle of Pinot Meunier, with 5% of the base wine barrel fermented. This won’t be made every year. Fewer than 3000 bottles made, retail £80 in the UK. [Interesting note: I did a google search and found out that the IWSC gave this a Bronze medal, which I reckon is a miscarriage of justice.]

Black Chalk HiDE Extra Brut 2021 Hampshire, England
12% alcohol. Single vineyard, stony soils, planted in 2011. 48% Pinot Noir, 47% Chardonnay, 5% Pinot Meunier. Partial malolactic fermentation, 5% barrel ferment. 46 months on lees and at least 6 months on cork post-disgorgement. 9.1 g/litre acid and a residual sugar level of 4.2 g/l (not always the same as dosage). Ripe, complex nose of apple, pear and honey, with a hint of toast. The palate is concentrated and complex with lemon and apple fruit and some toastiness, with a mid-palate richness but then finishing fresh with a nice acid line. This is very much in the Black Chalk style, with nice purity and freshness, but there are also extra dimensions here. Really impressive. 94/100

title: The Central Dozen, an important exercise in telling the contemporary story of Central Otago Pinot Noir through a curated selection of 12 bottles
summary: Website: https://www.centralotagowine.co/initiatives/centraldozen I’m a big fan of Pinot Noir from Central Otago in New Zealand. I’ve visited numerous times, and
content:
Website: https://www.centralotagowine.co/initiatives/centraldozen

I’m a big fan of Pinot Noir from Central Otago in New Zealand. I’ve visited numerous times, and I like the way that there’s now a good stylistic spread. I was recently sent a case of 12 examples from the 2024 vintage, called Central Dozen.

This is a selection of twelve Pinot Noir drawn from across Central Otago. The selection was made by  Emma Jenkins, with local winemakers Jen Parr, Greg Lane and Sam Davies. They blind tasted their way through 76 wines to a shortlist of 19. Then they whittled this down to the final dozen looking for wines that reflected the essence of the season.

Some of my pics from various visits:

This is a beautiful region, but it’s also quite a small one, with just over 2000 hectares planted. 

Pinot Noir dominates plantings, mainly because it does so well. There are 1765 hectares of Pinot here, with Pinot Gris (170 ha) and Chardonnay (105 ha) taking the podium places. Then there’s 54 hectares of Riesling, 40 hectares of Sauvignon Blanc and 30 hectares of ‘others’.

These are the wines I tried. It wasn’t meant to be a selection of the very ‘best’ wines from the region, but more a set of Pinots that capture the place and the season.

Amisfield Pinot Noir 2024 Pisa
Amisfield have 85 hectares of vines with 55 hectares of vines planted between 1999 and 2018, with a mix of clones (667, 115, 777, UCD5 & 6, and Abel) and rootstocks. Soils vary between gravelly lochar soils and wind-blown loess, and heavier silt-clay Waenga soils. The entire vineyard was certified organic in 2021. Harvested 18 March & 13 April. Organic, average vine ages 23 years. A mix of wild and inoculated fermentations, 10-15% whole bunch, 20% new oak. This is supple and sweetly fruited with appealing cherry and strawberry fruit. Rich, smoothly textured and quite refined. The sweet fruit dominates, with nice texture and a subtly spicy framing. It delivers some complexity and a lot of pleasure, with a sweet core of fruit. 93/100

Burn Cottage Moonlight Race Pinot Noir 2024
Harvested 30 March – 15 April. A blend of Lowburn and Bannockburn fruit, from four organic vineyards. Vine age 9-25 years.  Wild ferment, 6% whole bunch, 19% new oak. This is stylish and assertive, with bright red fruits to the fore. There’s a brightness and energy to this wine, with subtle tarry reductive hints and a touch of savoury iodine/blood character framing the sleek red cherry fruit, with some crunchy raspberry and just a bit of tannin. This combines the approachability of sweet red fruits with a touch of seriousness and some structure to really good effect. There’s just a touch of wood spice in the mix, too. Very stylish. 94/100

Dicey The Inlet Pinot Noir 2024 Bannockburn
Harvested 7 & 13 April. Vine age 20 years. Wild ferment and 16 months in used French oak. 20% whole bunch. This is fresh and supple with sweet red cherry and cranberry fruit, with some nice wild strawberry notes, a touch of spice and a bit of grippy tannin. This has some generosity to the fruit, but stays fresh and quite elegant. There’s texture and purpose here, with lovely fruit purity and ease. 93/100

Grasshopper Rock Block 6 Pinot Noir 2024 Alexandra
Harvested 6–10 & 18 April. Average vine age 23 years. A mix of wild and inoculated ferment, no whole bunch, 13 months ageing in French oak, 25% new. This has really intriguing aromatics with some peppery spiciness and hints of blood as well as floral cherry and berry fruits, as well as a touch of pot Pourri. The palate is fresh and expressive with some herby notes accompanying textured cherry and berry fruits. It has massive drinkability, but there’s also some structure and complexity. Stylish and compelling. 94/100

Maude Estate Single Vineyard Poison Creek Pinot Noir 2024 Cental Otago
This is from Queensberry, which is a part of Central Otago you get to after passing Pisa but before you reach Wanaka, on the same bank of Lake Dunstan. Harvested 18 April, average vine age 23 years, wild ferment, 25% new oak, 36% whole bunch. Warm, spicy nose with sweet cherry and berry fruits. The palate has textured, warm, spicy berry fruits with a bit of spicy oak in the mix. There’s a lovely richness to this wine, but also definition and focus. Really nice depth and harmony with lots of sweet fruit. 94/100

Moko Hills Pinot Noir 2024 Bendigo
Harvested 3 & 9 April, average vine age 9 years, wild ferment with 40% whole bunch, 12 months in French oak (15% new). This is bright, crunchy and juicy, with a spicy, savoury edge to the focused cherry and berry fruits. There’s some grainy structure here: it’s very Bendigo in style, with the warmth giving a bit more tannic intensity. Grainy and detailed, with some sour cherry on the finish. 93/100

Mora Vale Pinot Noir 2024 Pisa
13.7% alcohol. Harvested 9 April, 33 year old vines, clone 115, inoculated ferment, 20% whole bunch, 30% new oak. This is a beautifully delicate Pinot Noir with bright strawberry and raspberry fruit, with a bit of raspy tannin and nice juiciness. This tends to freshness and elegance, and the new oak adds a nice spicy twist to the berry fruits. Lovely stuff, with brightness and energy. I think this has the potential to develop, and it would be nice to see the oak integrate a bit more. 93/100

Ted by Mount Edward Central Otago Pinot Noir 2024 Central Otago
Organic, 20 year old (average) vines. Wild ferment, 15% new oak, no whole bunch. Fresh, linear and sappy on the nose with juicy cherry and cranberry fruit. There’s nice freshness on the palate with some green hints sitting under textured strawberry and cranberry fruit, with hints of reduction as well as supple fruit. There’s a slight grainy, reductive edge to this wine, but it works really well. Lovely red fruit focus to this wine. 93/100

Mt Difficulty Bannockburn Pinot Noir 2024 Bannockburn
Harvested 13 March – 17 April, average vine age 24 years. Wild ferment with a bit of inoculation where needed, 10% whole bunch. 20% new oak. This is sleek and ripe with lovely cherry and plum fruit. Textured and appealing with a core of sweet fruit, and then some fine spicy notes. There’s a richness at the heart of this wine, with some stewed strawberry, cherry and raspberry, as well as a hint of spicy oak. Really well put together. 93/100 (£31 Waitrose in the UK)

Pyramid Valley Low Burn Pinot Noir 2024 Lowburn
13.5% alcohol. Loess over compacted lakebed silts with some pedogenic limestone. The old Lowburn Ferry property. Harvested 4-16 April, organic farming, 20% 21 year old vines (the original plantings), 80% 4 year old vines (new plantings post purchase). Wild ferment, 2.5% whole bunch, 17% new oak. This is quite aromatic with floral red cherry and dried herb notes, and it’s quite alluring with the sweet fruit. On the palate this is silky and textured with real harmony to the cherry and berry fruits, and some fine spicy detail, finishing with a sappy green hint that’s quite lovely. It’s a pure, voluminous, silky and textural Pinot Noir that’s elegant and very fine. Not as profound as some of the Pyramid wines from North Canterbury, but so delicious. 95/100

Valli Gibbston Pinot Noir 2024 Gibbston
6 harvest passes between 7 – 22 April. Combination of indigenous and inoculated fermentation. Vine age 24 and 5 years. 24% whole bunch, aged 11 months in 25% new French barriques. Beautifully floral on the nose with red cherries, berries, some floral notes, a touch of white pepper and some sagebrush/dried mountain herbs. The palate is superbly elegant. It’s fresh and light but has good concentration of flavour, with a liqueur-like richness to the red fruits and silky texture. Just enough tannin to keep it serious. A beautiful expression of Gibbston. 95/100

Wild Irishman Tūturi Pinot Noir 2024 Alexandra
Tuturi is the Wild Irishman home vineyard. It’s a 2.5 ha site planted in 2002/2003 with clones 115 and 667, on deep alluvial gravels. Wild Irishman is the latest venture of the pioneering winemaker, Alan Brady, who established Gibbston Valley Wines in 1983 before setting up Mount Edward in 1997. After “unsuccessfully retiring” in 2005, Alan developed Wild Irishman with fellow Irishman and winemaker, Brian Shaw in 2021, building his third winery at the age of 85. Both ‘wild Irishman’ and the te reo Maori ‘tuturi’ are names for the native thorny shrub matagouri that is common in the region. Harvested 6 and 13 April from vines planted in 2002. Wild ferment, no whole bunch, 11 months in French oak barrels, 20% new. This has alluring aromatics of black cherries, some wood spice, and some iodine/blood/iron savouriness. There’s a touch of reduction. The palate shows great concentration, and a really wide dynamic range, from some sweet, lush black fruit character, then some silkiness, and then some grunty structure. This gives some tension. There’s a freshness and juiciness to this wine, but also some seriousness. It will be interesting to watch it evolve over the next few years. 95/100

title: Polish wine exploration: Winnica Moderna (updated with fresh notes, 2026)
summary: Website: https://www.winnicamoderna.pl/ Winnica Moderna is based in Poland’s Lower Silesian region, which is one of the warmest parts of the
content:
Website: https://www.winnicamoderna.pl/

Winnica Moderna is based in Poland’s Lower Silesian region, which is one of the warmest parts of the country. Their vineyards are in the Trzebnickie Hills, and I tasted the wines with owner Nestor Kościański (pictured below).

Notes from 2026:

Winnica Moderna Pet Nat ‘F*ck the Frost’ 2024 Poland
80% Rondo, 20% Johanniter. A big spring frost meant harvest was only 20% of normal. Orange-pink in colour with lovely brightness and texture. Notes of pear, orange peel and nice herbal hints. 90/100

Winnica Moderna See You in Hell Brut Nature NV Poland
Riesling, base year 2019, 2 years in tank, bottled 2021, recently disgorged. Vivid and intense with nice acidity and sweet citrus fruit. Dry with a great acid line. 91/100

Winnica Moderna See You in My Life NV Poland
Rondo, base wine 2021, bottled 2022, disgorged November 2025. Zero dosage but residual sugar of 9 g/litre. Lovely citrus, with some stylish pear fruit, and notes of cherry and almond. Smoky and spicy with some toasty notes. 91/100

Winnica Moderna Johanniter Muscaris Skin Contact 2024 Poland
This is an orange wine, with the only addition a little SO2 before bottling. Full yellow colour with lovely fruit, and a nice pithy note under the pear and peach fruit. Nice acid line and good balance. 92/100

Winnica Moderna Johanniter Orange 2023 Poland
Just a small SO2 addition before bottling. Full yellow in colour with nice tangy citrus fruit with a touch of orange peel. Nice weight and good acidity. 92/100

Winnica Moderna Pinot Noir 2023 Poland
10 days on skins then malolactic in stainless steel, then 300 litre used French oak. Pale red colour. Delicate, sweet strawberry and red cherry fruit. Light, with some spicy detail. Lovely stuff. 92/100

Notes from January 2025

Winnica Moderna Pet Nat 2023 Silesia, Poland
This is a blend of Johanniter, Riesling and Scheurebe, and it’s a brut nature. It’s undisgorged. They split the juice into two, fermenting on portion then adding the remainder (which has been kept in a fridge) on bottling. This is fruity, lively and bright with nice energy and good acidity. Juicy, bright and alive, this is limey with lovely purity and texture. Serious. 92/100

Winnica Moderna Pet Nat Rosé 2023 Silesia, Poland
This is 80% Rondo and 20% Pinot Gris. Fruity and lively with good acidity, this shows textured cherry, pear and lime fruit. Zesty and alert with lovely fruit. 90/100

Winnica Moderna Chardonnay Sur Lie 2022 Silesia, Poland
13% alcohol. Stainless steel. This is fruity and lively with apples, wax and pear. Shows nice texture and depth with a hint of almond. Fine and expressive. 90/100

Winnica Moderna Chardonnay Sur Lie & Barrique 2022 Silesia, Poland
Complex with almond and woody notes, as well as bold, textured pear and peach fruit. Nice density and fruit intensity, with a savoury twist. 90/100

Winnica Moderna Pinot Noir 2022 Silesia, Poland
Sandy clay soils in lower Silesia, with 3.1 hectares of vines. They grow both vinifera and resistant varieties, with a focus on vinifera, including Riesling and Pinot Noir. This Pinot is made from French clones. 10 days on skins, 14 months in used oak. Juicy, bright and pure with nice focused red cherry and raspberry fruit. It’s quite fresh and very focused with lovely direct fruit. Lovely purity to the fruit with some elegance, although it’s a tiny bit rigid and hollow on the mid-palate. But really impressive and pure, with high acid apparent. The fruit is fully ripe, though. 92/100

Winnica Moderna Cabernet Cortis 2022 Silesia, Poland
Chalky, gravelly nose with a hint of beetroot. Lovely weight on the palate, with chalky, spicy notes showing nice weight and some grippy character, as well as some green hints. Mouthfilling and satisfying. 91/100

title: A big tasting of Tenerife wines, with some nice surprises
summary: As part of the recent Island Wines Summit in Tenerife we had a chance to taste through a range of
content:
As part of the recent Island Wines Summit in Tenerife we had a chance to taste through a range of wines from the island, ordered by appellation. These are my notes. Missing here are any of the wines from Suertes del Marques, which I have written about in the past, and which are probably the best wines from the island.

DO Valle de la Orotava

El Roboso Blanco 2025 Valle de la Orotava
This is highly aromatic in a fresh, fruit-driven style with nice sweet citrus fruit and a touch of grapiness. Attractive in this style. 88/100

La Haya Barrica 2018 Valle de la Orotava
Quite old-school, barrel-aged white. Full gold in colour with some oxidative hints and some oak influence. Good in its style. 88/100

Salomé Tinto 2025 Valle de la Orotava
Supple and juicy with raspberry and cherry fruit as well as some grip. Nice ripeness, but also shows balance. Grainy and delicious. 92/100

La Araucaria Tinto 2022 Valle de la Orotava
Crunchy with some oak spice as well as direct berry fruits. Lots of barrel, but nice fruit here. 89/100

Engazo Tinto Cosecha 2023 Valle de la Orotava
A blend of Listan Negro, Tintilla and Castellana. Fresh and ripe with nice sweet rounded berry and cherry fruits, with a bit of grip but also some saltiness. A rich style, quite juicy, with some ripe strawberry too. 91/100

Murcal Tinto Barrica 2023 Valle de la Orotava
Grainy with nice sweet cherry and plum fruit, as well as some grip. Spicy and vivid with nice depth and structure. 90/100

DO Albona

Mencey Chasna Blanco Seco 2025 Albona
From 1300 m altitude. Very fruity and bright with good acidity under the grapefruit and lemon fruit. Crisp style. 89/100

Finca Encanto de Vilaflor Vilaflor de Chasna Listán Blanco 2024 Albona
From 1300 m. This is mineral and taut with some salty flor character. Lively and direct with lovely fruit. Very precise. 91/100

Bodega Arese Viña Arese Tinto 2025 Albona
Fruity and lively, pure and aromatic, with rounded fruit. Raspberry and almods notes. A nice fruity style. 92/100

Chasnero Tinto Ecológico 2025 Albona
Juicy, stony and mineral with a chalky edge to the vivid cherry fruit. Nice brightness here with massive drinkability and good fruit purity. 93/100

DO Tacoronte Acentejo

Marba Blanco 2025 Tacoronte-Acentejo
Bright and tart, juicy and fruity with nice balance. Linear. 88/100

Hacienda de Acentejo Tinto Joven 2025 Tacoronte-Acentejo
Juicy, bright and crisp with nice redcurrant and cherry fruit, as well as a touch of raspberry. Fresh and lively. 90/100

Viña Riquelas Tinto Negramoll 2024 Tacoronte-Acentejo
Nice intensity with tart, bright cherry and raspberry fruit, showing nice grip. Has freshness but also some substance. Good energy, and a hint of green. 93/100

Viña Estévez Tinto Barrica 2024 Tacoronte-Acentejo
Juicy and bright with nice vibrant raspberry and cherry fruit as well as a slight saltiness. There’s good intensity, and there’s also a touch of oak. 91/100

DO Ycoden-Daute-Isora

Artifice Listán Blanco 2023 Ycoden-Daute-Isora
Stony, mineral and long with lovely presence to the fruit. Mineral and saline with a slight wildness. So expressive. 94/100

Artifice Tinto 2023 Ycoden-Daute-Isora
Juicy and fresh with redcurrant fruit and some fresh red cherries. Fruity but also has some blood and iron notes. Focused with nice texture, and herbal and redcurrant notes on the finish. 94/100

DO Islas Canarias

Piedra Fluida Los Frontones 2023 Islas Canarias Tenerife
From the highest vineyard on the island at 1650 m. Stony and salty; mineral and incisive with high acidity. Really intense with a stony finish to the citrus fruit. Distinctive and lovely. 94/100

Vinatiago Listán Blanco de Canarias 2025 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Ungrafted vines (very common on Tenerife). Concentrated and fruit-driven. Linear with lovely intensity, and a saline edge to the pear and citrus fruit. Good depth of fruit to this wine. 94/100

Linage del Pago Vino de Parcela Marmajuelo 2024 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Grapey and salty with nice intensity. Vivid and saline with good depth and some bold flavours. 94/100

El Sitio Malvasía Aromática Vino de la Parcela Bebedros 2024 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Pithy and intense with some grapiness on the nose. Powerful and rich on the palate with some terpenic character and good fruit. Has some energy. 92/100

Atrevino Listán Negro 2022 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Fresh and light. Juicy with some redcurrant and strawberry fruit. Shows elegance, and a dark, stony, crushed rock character as well as a saline twist. 93/100

Taginaste Can 2024 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Listán Negro and Vijariego. Some noticeable oak influence here. Classically structured with some berry and cherry fruit and a stony twist. 90/100

Envinate Benje Tinto 2023 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Linear, stony and bright with juicy redcurrant fruit. Tart and linear with some blood and iodine notes in the mix. Really focused. 94/100

Bodega El Lomo Listán Negro 2024 Islas Canarias Tenerife
Supple and juicy with nice red cherry and redcurrant fruit. Stony, with some saltiness and elegance. Lighter-style red with some presence, this is quite stylish. 93/100

Wild Irishman Tūturi Pinot Noir 2024 Alexandra, Central Otago, New Zealand

title: Canada’s Okanagan and Similkameen Valleys (15) Meyer Family Vineyards
summary: Website: https://mfvwines.com/ Jak and Janice Meyer are turning out some of the best Chardonnay and Pinot Noir in the Okanagan.
content:
Website: https://mfvwines.com/

Jak and Janice Meyer are turning out some of the best Chardonnay and Pinot Noir in the Okanagan. 2006 was their first vintage, released in spring 2008. ‘The original plan was this was a hobby on the side,’ says Jak. ‘Custom crush, having a bit of fun.’ In a prior life he was a stockbroker and then he moved to mergers and acquisitions: wine was never supposed to be a serious second career.

They custom crushed 2006 and 2007, and in 2008 they started making their wines at Lake Breeze. They hired Chris Carson who’d worked in New Zealand. They bought their winery and tasting room in December 2008.

In 2008 they made 700 cases from 4 acres of vines. Jak realised selling wine is hard, as well as making it, and he knew that at this size they’d never make any money. But by this stage he’d got the bug. This was a fun business, so they decided to grow. A property (now their home farm) came up after the financial crash, with 16 acres of vineyards, and they were in business. Every couple of years they added a new building to the property and it built up.

Most fermentations are wild yeast for both Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. In 2024 because of the lack of grapes they did a Chardonnay and some rosé from Washington State in 2024. In a normal year, production is around 8000 cases.

In the vineyards they have around 15% loss from the 2024 freeze. But it would have been a lot more if there hadn’t been a shortage of vines at the nurseries. 75% of those replaced would have survived, says Jak, after seeing what he thought were dead vines bounce back, sending suckers up in July and August.

The home farm has 11 acres of Pinot Noir, 3 acres of Chardonnay and 1.5 acres of Gewurztraminer.

Meyer Chardonnay 2024 Colombia River Plateau, Washington State
Bought some Chardonnay juice from Washington. This is fresh and supple with nice pure citrus and pear fruit as well as a bit of white peach. Nicely textured and fruit driven. 89/100 ($21)

Meyer Old Main Road Chardonnay 2023 Naramata Bench
13.5% alcohol. 25% new oak, 11 months in barrel. Toast, meal and spice on the nose with some ripe peach and pear fruit. The palate is supple and bright with lovely fruit presence. Nice energy as well as some depth and a bit of stoniness. Really stylish. 93/100 ($32)

Meyer McClean Creek Road Chardonnay 2023 Okanagan Falls
13.5% alcohol. This is the home property. This is linear and focused with nice density and weight, with some pear and peach as well as hints of nut and meal. Nice balance with good acidity under the fruit. Seamless but with some density, this is very stylish. 94/100 ($32)

Meyer Micro Cuvée Chardonnay Old Main Road Vineyard 2022 Naramata Bench
13.5% alcohol. This can come from either of the two properties. It’s a barrel selection. 50% new oak, 100% malolactic. Lovely concentration and intensity. This is vivid and linear with powerful, lively citrus and white peach fruit, with a stony linearity. Juicy, bright and focused with nice acidity on the finish. This is still tight and primary. 95/100 ($61)

Meyer Pinot Noir 2023 Okanagan Valley
This comes from Naramata, Osoyoos, Kaleden (west side of the Lake, 4 acres of Pinot, they bought it recently), OK Falls. Bright, supple and enjoyable with some fine spices under the floral, sweet fruit. There’s nice concentration, a bit of meatiness, and nice fine spicy detail. Very stylish and enjoyable. 93/100 ($25)

Meyer McLean Creek Road Vineyard Pinot Noir 2023 Okanagan Falls
20% new oak. This has nice density with a savoury, spicy twist to the nicely concentrated cherry and raspberry fruit, with really nice texture: it’s silky, but there’s some spicy structure, too. This has pleasure but also seriousness. 95/100 ($38)

Meyer Old Block Pinot Noir McLean Creek Vineyard 2022 Okanagan Falls
13.5% alcohol. Planted in 1994, 40% new oak. Light in colour. So elegant, fine and refined with beautiful red cherry and raspberry fruit, and a touch of cranberry. Such elegance and finesse with real purity and layers of flavour. Remarkable elegance to this wine. Thrilling, relying on elegance rather than power. Floral, ethereal. 95/100 ($48)

Meyer Micro Cuvée Pinot Noir McLean Creek Vineyard 2022 Okanagan Falls
13.5% alcohol. 91 (Pommard) and 115 clones. Relatively pale in colour. Elegant but with some structure, showing nice purity and finesse, with some spicy, white pepper detail. Nice finesse with some iodine and blood hints around the edge of the sweet red cherry and cranberry fruit. Fine and fresh on the finish. 95/100 ($61)

title: Rheingau Riesling: tasting through some of the best examples at the VDP tasting 2026
summary: Continuing with my write ups from the amazing VDP tastings in Weisbaden, August 2026, here are notes on the Rheingau
content:
Continuing with my write ups from the amazing VDP tastings in Weisbaden, August 2026, here are notes on the Rheingau Rieslings I tasted. It’s clear from the scores that I liked these wines quite a bit.

August Kesseler Riesling Lorchhausen SELIGMACHER 2025 Rheingau
Focused lime-laden nose with nice precision. The palate is pure, crystalline and focused with good acidity and almost perfect balance. 95/100

Prinz Riesling Rüdesheim BERG SCHLOSSBERG 2025 Rheingau
Chiselled and bright with lovely pure lemony fruit, showing delicacy and a chalky minerality. Quite lovely. 95/100

August Kesseler Riesling Rüdesheim BERG ROSENECK 2025 Rheingau
Linear, bright and precise with great fruit purity. Lemon and lime with some pretty florals, and keen acidity. Such precision here. 94/100

Josef Spreitzer Riesling Mittelheim SANKT NIKOLAUS 2025 Rheingau
Some wood evident here. A very different style of Riesling with lots of texture and depth. Nice citrus and pear fruit. Unusual. 92/100

Josef Spreitzer Riesling Oestrich ROSENGARTEN 2025 Rheingau
Lively and juicy with nice texture to the citrus fruit, and good acidity. Has presence and some mid-palate depth. 93/100

Prinz Riesling Hallgarten JUNGFER 2025 Rheingau
Bold with nice fruit intensity. Ripe citrus and pear. Lovely depth to this wine, finishing spicy and chalky. 92/100

Barth Riesling Hallgarten SCHÖNHELL 2025 Rheingau
Textural and quite bold with rich, ripe citrus fruit and some pear and apple richness. Midweight and appealing. 92/100

Barth Riesling Hattenheim HASSEL 2025 Rheingau
Lots of presence here: bold and characterful with intense citrus fruit as well as some pear skin richness. Has density and good acidity. 93/100

Prinz Riesling Hattenheim NUSSBRUNNEN 2025 Rheingau
Nice acid line with a chalky edge to the citrus fruit. Has nice intensity with some grip. Zippy and linear. 93/100

Josef Spreitzer Riesling Hattenheim WISSELBRUNNEN 2025 Rheingau
Rich and harmonious with nice texture, and a lovely mineral undertow to the ripe citrus fruit. This has presence and depth. So refined. 95/100

Prinz Riesling Erbach MARCOBRUNN 2025 Rheingau
Midweight and nicely textured with ripe citrus fruit and a hint of orange peel and melon richness. 92/100

Robert Weil Riesling Kiedrich GRÄFENBERG 2025 Rheingau
Focused and compact with taut citrus fruit. Lovely balance to this wine with everything in place. Still primary. 94/100

Domdechant Werner Riesling Hochheim KIRCHENSTÜCK 2025 Rheingau
Juicy and linear with bright lemon and lime fruit. Nice precision and focus with lovely detail to the zippy fruit. Crystalline. 94/100

Domdechant Werner Riesling Hochheim HÖLLE 2025 Rheingau
Honied and floral on the nose with lovely juiciness to the crystalline citrus fruit, and a hint of apple. Pretty wine. 93/100

Joachim Flick Riesling Hochheim KÖNIGIN VICTORIABERG DECHANTENRUHE 2025 Rheingau
Chalky and mineral with nice precision and lovely fruit weight. Has some freshness and nice texture. Crystalline finish. Open, with nice balance. 93/100

Joachim Flick Riesling Wicker NONNBERG VIER MORGEN 2025 Rheingau
This is nicely fruity with good weight. Appealing style showing nice freshness and focus. Has some detail to it. Lemons and apples. 93/100

Geheimrat J. Wegeler Riesling Rüdesheim BERG SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Rheingau
Lively citrus nose with real impact. The palate is really bright and zesty with crisp lemony fruit and high acidity. Distinctive. 93/100

Peter Jakob Kühn Riesling Rüdesheim BERG SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Rheingau             
Bright and linear showing chiselled citrus fruit with keen acidity. Brisk in style with lots of impact. Impressive in this bright, linear style. 94/100

Balthasar Ress Riesling Rüdesheim BERG ROTTLAND 2024 Rheingau              
Juicy, linear but with some nice pear and peach richness as well as a core of linear citrus fruit. Stylish and layered, showing nice complexity. 94/100

Geheimrat J. Wegeler Riesling Rüdesheim BERG ROTTLAND 2024 Rheingau
Compact, taut and linear with bright, pure lemony fruit. Very primary. 92/100

Geheimrat J. Wegeler Riesling Geisenheim ROTHENBERG 2024 Rheingau
Juicy, bright, zesty and pure with nice precision to the focused citrus fruit. Very lemony and quite intriguing. 94/100

Geheimrat J. Wegeler Riesling Geisenheim MORSCHBERG 2024 Rheingau
Slightly honied nose leads to a lean, almost austere palate showing focused lemony fruit. 91/100

Schloss Johannisberg Riesling Johannisberg SCHLOSS JOHANNISBERG 2024 Rheingau
Compact, linear and pure with bright lemony fruit. Primary, showing potential. 94/100

Prinz von Hessen Riesling Johannisberg KLAUS 2024 Rheingau
Juicy, crystalline and linear with appealing lemony fruit. Has nice weight and balance. Pure and vivid. 93/100

Geheimrat J. Wegeler Riesling Winkel JESUITENGARTEN 2024 Rheingau
Stony and lemony with bright fruit and good acidity. Compact. 92/100

Prinz von Hessen Riesling Winkel HASENSPRUNG 2024 Rheingau     
Nice focus to this with pretty lemony fruit and some chalky mineral undertones. Bright and primary. 93/100

Peter Jakob Kühn Riesling Mittelheim SANKT NIKOLAUS 2024 Rheingau
So bright and lemony with nice intensity to the chalk-laden minerally palate. Pristine fruit here with potential for development. 95/100

Peter Jakob Kühn Riesling Hallgarten JUNGFER 2024 Rheingau
Lovely tension here. There’s a floral quality to the citrus fruits on the nose, and then in the mouth this is mineral and layered, with good acidity. Amazing dynamic range. 96/100

Geheimrat J. Wegeler Riesling Oestrich DOOSBERG 2024 Rheingau
Bright, juicy, primary and lemony with pure fruit. 91/100

Peter Jakob Kühn Riesling Oestrich DOOSBERG 2024 Rheingau
This is alert and crystalline with lovely detail to the bright lemon and lime fruit. There’s an extra dimension here, with fine spicy detail. 94/100

Balthasar Ress Riesling Hattenheim WISSELBRUNNEN 2024 Rheingau
Some honey and wax on the nose as well as ripe citrus. The palate is bold and textural with nice intensity and depth. Quite serious with good weight to the fruit. 94/100

Kaufmann Riesling Hattenheim WISSELBRUNNEN 2024 Rheingau
Chiselled and linear but also with depth and richness of fruit. A complete Riesling, showing some pear and peac richness as well as crystalline fruit. 95/100

Diefenhardt Riesling Rauenthal IM ROTHENBERG 2024 Rheingau
Nice precision and complexity here with crystalline lemony fruit, and great balanced between the richness and the acidity. Lovely. 94/100

Diefenhardt Riesling Martinsthal LANGENBERG 2024 Rheingau
Compact and lemony with some apple and pear notes as well as bright citrus fruit. Stylish and fruit-laden. 93/100

title: Canada’s Okanagan and Similkameen Valleys (14) Nostalgia
summary: Website: https://nostalgiawines.ca/ Gina Fernandes Harfman is the owner and winemaker at Nostalgia Wines, based in Black Sage Bench in Canada’s
content:
Website: https://nostalgiawines.ca/

Gina Fernandes Harfman is the owner and winemaker at Nostalgia Wines, based in Black Sage Bench in Canada’s Okanagan Valley. This is an innovative project that’s very design led. She has Portuguese roots, but her family are fourth generation in the Okanagan.

An Okanagan local, Gina attended Fine Art school in Kelowna, and then did airbrush courses in Las Vegas, where she got work airbrushing and pinstriping hot rods and motorcycles. This has influenced the design of the labels.

It was in 2009 that she made her first wine, using some grapes from her father Ken Harfman’s vineyard in 2009 for a family event. This led her to enroll in Okanagan College to learn more about wine.

She did vintage at Oliver Twist winery in 2010, and in 2012 at the age of 32 she bought the winery, changing the name to Nostalgia Wines.

She has 17 acres of vines  and also purchases from her father, who has 16 acres on Osooyos. The wines are made on site, and she also does some custom crush.

The freezes hit hard. She lost 35% of production in December 2022, and lost another 30% in 2024. She’s now replanting and changing some of the varieties.

To make up for the 2024 shortfall she bought in 5000 litres of juice from Washington State. Okanagan legend Mike Bartier arranged for juice to be brought in for a number of wineries. He also looks after the vineyard here. Interestingly, her father didn’t lose anything in Osooyos.

85% of sales are direct to consumer. The pin-up series has six different wines, and these are all blends. Classic cars are also a focus here and they’ve tapped into this market.

In the vineyard she has a new electric frost fan that is much more economical to run, which she got through a government grant.

Nostalgia Sauvignon Blanc 2024 Horse Heaven Hills
From Prosser, Washington. Stainless steel, cultured yeast. Supple, fresh and ripe with nice sweet pear and cherry, as well as a touch of grapefruit. Nicely textured with some ripeness. This offers a lot of pleasure. 89/100

Nostalgia Kerner 2022 Okanagan
This is bright with nice texture and energy, showing sweet pear and citrus fruit with a hint of melony richness. There’s a touch of aniseed, too, with a bit of mandarin. This has lovely weight to it, finishing fresh. 91/100

Nostalgia Chardonnay 2022 Okanagan
This is the Family Collection Chardonnay (black label) and has some nice oak use supporting the pear and peach fruit, with some nice spicy detail. Nicely balanced. 90/100

Nostalgia Gamay Rosé 2023 Okanagan
Smoky juice, treated with carbon, but you’d never know! Osooyos, direct pressed. Juicy and focused with nice bright citrus and cherry fruit. This is energetic and bright with a slight saltiness. Very stylish with lovely flavours. 92/100

Nostalgia Rockabilly Red 2022 Okanagan
This is a Bordeaux-style blend with some Syrah. Staves in tank. Lovely balance here with some pepper and wood spice notes under the crunchy raspberry and cherry fruit. Shows lovely balance with a crowd-pleasing character but also a hint of seriousness. 92/100

Nostalgia Meritage 2019 Okanagan
13.3% alcohol. Cabernet Sauvignon dominant (from Osooyos). Aged 17 months in barrels (80% French oak, 20% American, 30% new). Nice concentration and freshness here with some spicy detail to the berry and black fruits, with some nice structure. Grippy with nice intensity to the fruit, and a dry, tannic finish that works really well. 93/100

Nostalgia Meritage 2020 Okanagan
Merlot dominant this year. Really nice balance to this wine with well structured black cherry and blackberry fruit, with a bit of grip. Has a peppery edge to the fruit. Juicy but with density, and some nice grip. This is really good. 93/100

Nostalgia Cherry Baby
16% alcohol. 60% cherry, 40% merlot. Old cherry varieties. Cherries are frozen to help maceration. They are pressed, yeast is added, then it’s fortified twice. The Merlot has some sugar added to create alcohol and then it’s fermented, fortified and the two are blended. Solera system. This has spice, wood, sour cherry, a hint of raisin, and then some prune and chocolate. Mellow with a nice tangy edge from the cherries. Not too sweet. Some cherry pit notes, too. 90/100

title: Highlights: Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Trans-Douro-Express Cima Corgo 2022 Douro
summary: I recently reviewed the amazing wines from Mateus Nicolau de Almeida. Douro with a difference, packaged in Riesling-style bottles, aiming
content:
I recently reviewed the amazing wines from Mateus Nicolau de Almeida. Douro with a difference, packaged in Riesling-style bottles, aiming at elegance. This is one of a series of three wines looking at the different sub-regions of the Douro, and it’s really good, and not expensive. I bought this from a wine bar in Peso de Regua.

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Trans-Douro-Express Cima Corgo 2022 Douro
12.5% alcohol. This is full flavoured but beautifully balanced with fresh, fragrant red cherry and plum fruit, as well as a bit of raspberry crunch. There’s some wet stone minerality here, and it finishes fresh. A classic Douro red with real poise and detail, and a delightful sappy green hint on the finish. 93/100 (€16 in Portugal)

And here’s a note on the equivalent wine from Douro Superior:

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Trans-Douro-Express Douro Superior 2022 Douro
12.5% alcohol. This is so fresh and vital, with a lovely acid line under the bright raspberry and cherry fruit. There’s some tannic crunch here, but the fruit isn’t at all underripe. Very al dente in style, and quite delicious, offering immediate pleasure but also some potential for development. 93/100 (€16 in Portugal)

title: Highlights: Rall Syrah 2024 Swartland, South Africa
summary: Donavan Rall’s wines have impressed me since I first tasted them 15 years ago. This Syrah is just beautiful. Rall
content:
Donavan Rall’s wines have impressed me since I first tasted them 15 years ago. This Syrah is just beautiful.

Rall Syrah 2024 Swartland, South Africa
13% alcohol. Aged in concrete. This is quite beautiful. Floral aromatics with a slight stony edge to the sweet black cherry and berry fruits. There’s a hint of green sappiness, but also some charcoal and wood smoke. Beguiling. The palate is fresh and supple with sweet, alluring black cherry fruit, a hint of savoury olive tapenade, and also a bit of black pepper. There’s some subtle bloodiness, and a slight saltiness on the finish. Very Crozes-Hermitage from the flat lands in style, and deeply satisfying and delicious. The florals are probably more Côte-Rôtie: it’s very hard not to draw a northern Rhône parallel here. I bought two bottles, and my regret is not buying more. 95/100 (I bought this from The Wine Society in the UK)
